Welcome
Welcome to Claygate Primary School
We are delighted to welcome you to Claygate Primary School – a truly special place where every child is valued, supported and inspired to reach their full potential.
Claygate is a two-form entry primary school for children aged 4–11, with our nursery offering places for children aged 2–4. Rated Good, with areas judged as Outstanding, by Ofsted in 2023 and recognised within the top 5% of schools nationally for academic outcomes, we are a happy, thriving school community with a strong focus on achievement, personal growth, and well-being.
Our motto, ‘Together We Grow’, reflects the heart of our school. At Claygate, we combine high academic standards with exceptional pastoral care and an ambitious and broad programme of enrichment opportunities, helping every child develop confidence, curiosity, and a lifelong love of learning.
We are committed to nurturing each child’s individual talents so they flourish both academically and personally. Our dedication to personal development was recognised as Outstanding by Ofsted in 2023.
Our curriculum is ambitious for every child and carefully designed to prepare our children with the knowledge, skills, and character needed to thrive in today’s society. Based on the National Curriculum and personalised to our local area and needs, it is sequenced to build deep understanding, resilience, independence and a love of learning – qualities that support lifelong success.
A Beautiful Setting for Learning
Set within beautiful green surroundings, our extensive grounds provide endless opportunities for exploration, creativity and outdoor learning. From Forest School experiences to our unique indoor swimming pool, our children enjoy a wide range of enriching activities that enhance their education and broaden their horizons.
Learning within such peaceful natural surroundings helps our children develop meaningful connections with nature, fostering reflection, well-being and a sense of responsibility for the world around them.
Outstanding Early Years Provision
Our Early Years provision, including Acorns Nursery and Reception, was graded Outstanding by Ofsted. We are proud to provide children with the very best start to their education through exciting learning environments, carefully planned activities, and nurturing relationships that support every aspect of their development.
Visiting us is the best way to experience our warm and vibrant community, see our children engaged in their learning, meet our dedicated staff, and explore all that our wonderful school has to offer. Choosing the right school for your child is an important decision, and we would be delighted to welcome you to Claygate Primary School.

Our school governors are responsible for overseeing the management side of CPS ; strategy, policy, budgeting and staffing.
Our school governors are part of the largest volunteer force in the country - there are over a quarter of a million volunteers governing state funded schools in England.

Meet the Governors
Simon Tanner: co-Chair of Governors Profile
I live with my wife, Cath, and daughter, Sophie, in Claygate. My wife is a midwife at Kingston Hospital, and she also runs the Mums and Bumps group at Holy Trinity Church every Monday morning. Sophie is a TA at CPS. In my spare time I like to cycle, walk our two dogs and love live music. I attend Holy Trinity Church, Claygate, where I am a member of the PCC.
I have been a member of the Governing body since 2022 and was Vice Chair last year. I am an experienced commercial and financial adviser, having worked in a variety of roles across a broad spectrum of sectors and countries. I currently lead the Asset Transformation business at CBRE.
I am energised by working on things that genuinely make a difference and I love how central CPS is to the life of the village. Education is vitally important and I’m keen to help Claygate Primary School thrive and provide top quality education and facilities for the children of the village.
Meryl White: co-Chair of Governors Profile
I was born in Yorkshire and spent my working life in leadership roles in education and local government in the north of England, raising young people’s achievements and aspirations, starting out as a languages teacher and finishing my career as Director 11-19 Education. I moved to Claygate in 2020 to live near my family.
Since retiring, I became a cookery writer and presenter, sharing my passion for food history, inspired by my grandmother’s baking, on various online platforms.
I enjoy giving my time in the wider community and beyond. I am a keen member of the Claygate Gardening Society and sing my heart out with the Claygate Choral Society at Holy Trinity Church. My other activities include walking, swimming, playing the saxophone and reading. This summer, I was privileged to be a ‘Volontaire’ at the Paris 2024 Olympics and Paralympics, where I was in charge of a team of ‘Volontaires’ at the cycling Time Trials and Road Races.
I have been delighted to support Claygate Primary School as a Governor and Chair of Resources Committee since 2021, as a volunteer in the classroom and gardening with the children on the school allotment plots. I bring experience, intellectual commitment to achievement for all, value for relationships, boundless enthusiasm and pride in the success of pupils and staff.

Music
From September 2022, CPS has a brand new, bespoke Music Curriculum, which maximises our extensive instrumental resources in our Music Room and is adapted for each class in the school as they progress through it. Our Music curriculum is built upon the DfE's Model Music Curriculum 2021, the 2022 National Plan for Music Education, 'The Power of Music to Change Lives' and Ofsted's Music Subject Review 2023 'Striking the Right Note'. As they progress through the school, every pupil will experience, analyse and recreate music styles from throughout history and around the world; record music in writing using a variety of methods including staff notation; receive multiple opportunities to perform throughout their CPS career individually and within ensemble groups; and both improvise and compose extensively using voice and a variety of instruments.
An overview of each year group’s learning is attached below, along with the week-by-week learning progression throughout the year.
At CPS, we believe foundation subjects such as music and drama play a significant role in nurturing pupils' academic success across the whole curriculum. Current research in primary education offers support to this theory, and it is a view endorsed by the DfE in their use of practitioners employing music-centered schemes of education in a consultative capacity.
All classes from Year 1 upwards have a 45-minute Music lesson weekly throughout the year with a specialist primary music teacher, following a spiral progression commencing with discovering the basic elements of music-making in Year 1 and 2, through to developing these in the context of playing an instrument and discovering musical genres at Key Stage 2.
Throughout Key Stage 2, we offer progressive Whole Class Ensemble Tuition delivered by our own music specialist: pupils learn the recorder at Year 3; the junior saxophone at Year 4; the glockenspiel and keyboard family at Year 5 and the ukulele at Year 6.
In addition to the above, every class receives an additional 75 minutes of Music & Drama enrichment weekly for the duration of one half-term during the year. At Key Stage 1, this involves specialising in an instrument (Handbells at Year 1; Djembe drumming at Year 2), whilst at Key Stage 2, this focusses on drama and musical theatre skills, linking to the English curriculum and School's Voice 21 oracy status, as well as building self-esteem, confidence, articulation and self-expression. Every enrichment block culminates in a concluding performance to parents, carers and friends.
Every pupil also experiences a weekly singing assembly with material appropriate to their key stage. Alongside numerous traditional songs, we sing many bespoke songs written especially for our pupils, including celebrating our school values and learning environments. Senior pupils are often involved in composing the music and lyrics for these songs.
In Year 6, we have eight Music and Drama Champions, whose varied role includes leading singing assemblies and clubs for younger children; accompanying songs on the piano; caring for the Music Room and its resources; performing administrative and organisational roles for clubs and activities; and taking a lead role in presenting and narrating music and drama performances throughout the year. You will be able to spot our Music Champions from their distinctive treble clef badges!
To expand on our curriculum, pupils at Claygate can also attend one of our lunchtime or after school clubs – our Key Stage 2 Choir has performed at the OVO Wembley Arena, Dorking Halls, the Claygate Flower Show, the Village Christmas Lights Switch On and even taken part in a day at a recording studio, leading to a release of a new song to celebrate the life of Jane Goodall. Our Year 6 Music Champions are strongly involved in the KS1 choir, leading music games and warm-ups, and modelling good singing practice. This helps to create a real sense of connection between our oldest and youngest pupils, fostering musical ambition and aspiration. Our after school instrumental club offers Ukulele tuition, focusing on chords and strumming patterns as well as encouraging members to sing and accompany themselves.
Our pupils experience live orchestral performances at the Royal Festival Hall and drama workshops at local senior schools, and we also stage our own Year 6 Summer production, in which every pupil is invested, involved and invited to perform!
